title: Multiplication Anchors
summary: Use the facts you are sure of, times $2$, $5$ and $10$, as anchors to build the ones you are not: $7 \times 6 = 5 \times 6 + 2 \times 6$, $9 \times 8 = 10 \times 8 - 8$, and $23 \times 4 = 80 + 12$.
bigIdeas: Times $10$, times $5$ and times $2$ are anchors: build every other fact from them.
Split a number into parts, multiply each part, then add the answers.
tips: Times $5$ is half of times $10$: $14 \times 5$ is half of $140$, so $70$.
Six of something is five of it and one more: $7 \times 6 = 35 + 7 = 42$.
Times $9$ is times $10$ take one away: $9 \times 8 = 80 - 8 = 72$.
